name: Ariane 5
dispatch: Ariane 5 was the heavy-lift workhorse that carried European spaceflight to its peak — after one of the most famous failures in the field. Its 1996 maiden flight self-destructed 37 seconds up when guidance software inherited from Ariane 4 overflowed at the new rocket's higher speed, a software-engineering cautionary tale now taught worldwide. It recovered to become one of the most reliable heavy launchers ever built, lofting Rosetta, Galileo, BepiColombo, the ATV freighters to the ISS, and finally the James Webb Space Telescope — placed so precisely it saved years of the observatory's fuel.
description: ESA’s long-running heavy lifter, retired in 2023 after 117 launches. Carried Rosetta to comet 67P, JWST to L2, and dual-manifested geostationary commercial payloads for two decades.
